issues.legal_issue: A tenancy does not fall outside rent control merely because the landlord agrees to provide special amenities as part of a consolidated rent.
material_facts: Each tenancy covered a separately let room with associated facilities and fittings.
Under the lease, the landlord supplied electric current and other services and amenities as part of a consolidated monthly payment.
The tenants applied for fixation of standard rent under the rent-control legislation.
issues.conclusion: The legislation applied to the tenancies, and the consolidated payment for the premises and the special amenities was rent subject to control under the legislation.
issues.legal_principle: The broad definition of “premises” in section 2(8) of the West Bengal Premises Rent Control (Temporary Provisions) Act, 1950, and the Act’s purpose of controlling rents give its operative provisions wide application. The term “rent” includes payments for special amenities and services supplied under the letting, not merely payment for the building itself. The Court relied on Property Holding Co., Ltd. v. Clark and Alliance Property Co. Ltd. v. Shaffer, and rejected the contrary observation in Residence Ltd. v. Surendra Mohan.

predicates.rent_control_standardization_proceeding: A tenant sought standardization of rent under a rent-control process.
predicates.separately_let_building_part: The tenancy was of a separately let building or part of a building.
predicates.landlord_agreed_to_supply_amenities_for_: The landlord agreed to provide amenities or services as part of a consolidated payment for the letting.

issues.definition: When a tenant seeks rent standardization for a separately let building part and the consolidated payment includes landlord-provided amenities, the tenancy remains subject to rent control.

issues.legal_issue: Where no specific rent-fixation provision covers the circumstances of a consolidated rent, the fair and reasonable standard rent may be determined by considering all components of that rent and applying other relevant provisions where possible.
material_facts: The lease set one consolidated monthly rent that included electricity and other services and amenities.
The charges for electricity and government duty had increased, as had the cost of providing services and amenities.
The appellate authority considered those matters under the residuary provision and fixed a higher standard rent than the Rent Controller had fixed.
The figures fixed by the appellate authority were not challenged before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The residuary provision in section 9(g) applied. The appellate authority could consider all components of the agreed rent and relevant increases in determining a fair and reasonable standard rent, and its order was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9(g) of the West Bengal Premises Rent Control (Temporary Provisions) Act, 1950, permits standard rent to be fixed at a fair and reasonable rate where no other provision of the Act applies. The definition of standard rent in section 2(10) incorporates section 9 and Schedule A. In determining a fair and reasonable rent for a consolidated payment, the authorities may consider all its components and use other provisions of the Act to the extent they are applicable. The Court distinguished the contrary observation in Residence Ltd. v. Surendra Mohan and relied on the principles concerning the breadth of rent discussed in Property Holding Co., Ltd. v. Clark and Alliance Property Co. Ltd. v. Shaffer.

rule.if: rent_control_standardization_proceeding and consolidated_rent_includes_services and no_specific_fixation_provision_covers_circumstances and relevant_costs_increased

predicates.rent_control_standardization_proceeding: A tenant sought standardization of rent under a rent-control process.
predicates.consolidated_rent_includes_services: The agreed rent was a consolidated payment that included landlord-provided services or amenities.
predicates.no_specific_fixation_provision_covers_ci: No specific rent-fixation provision covered the circumstances requiring determination of standard rent.
predicates.relevant_costs_increased: The costs or charges associated with components of the consolidated rent had increased.

issues.definition: When a rent-standardization proceeding concerns a consolidated rent, no specific fixation provision covers the circumstances, and relevant costs have increased, a fair and reasonable standard rent may account for all rent components and those cost changes.

issues.legal_issue: A contention raised for the first time in the Supreme Court, which was not raised in the courts below, need not be considered.
material_facts: The landlord argued for the first time in the Supreme Court that the definition of premises did not apply and that a different statutory classification might apply.
That contention had not been raised in the courts below or in the statement of the case before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to consider the newly raised contention because it had not been advanced in the courts below.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the contention as too late to raise in that form because the cases had not been litigated on that ground. It also noted that the issue could be declined even assuming it required no fresh findings of fact.

predicates.supreme_court_appeal: The matter was before the Supreme Court on appeal.
predicates.contention_not_raised_in_lower_courts: A party advanced a contention in the Supreme Court that had not been raised in the courts below.

issues.definition: In a Supreme Court appeal, a contention not raised in the courts below may be declined.
